topics.title: Stern Discusses Offensive Letters
topics.summary: Howard Stern reads a collection of hateful letters he receives, frequently employing offensive language directed towards Jewish people and minority groups while expressing frustration with perceived attempts to limit his speech.

topics.title: Tom Snyder’s Frustration with a Television Deal
topics.summary: During an interview, Howard Stern expresses extreme frustration with Tom Snyder over a television deal gone wrong. Stern felt mocked by Snyder's analogies and demanded the show be pulled due to perceived deception and concerns about negative publicity.

topics.title: Teenage Angst and Subway Dog Death
topics.summary: A troubled teenager vents about his difficult life – school problems, family issues, and a general sense of alienation. He then shifts to discussing the ongoing investigation into the death of a subway dog, expressing skepticism while revealing unsettling personal thoughts and anxieties regarding violence.

topics.title: Subway Dog Death Probe & Police Reactions
topics.summary: An investigation is underway regarding the death of a dog during a subway incident, fueled by witness testimony and concerns about police conduct. The probe focuses on a homeless man, Robin, who was fatally burned in what appears to be a high-speed chase, raising questions about excessive force and potential biases within the response.

topics.title: Racial Concerns and High-Speed Chase
topics.summary: During the broadcast, the host expresses extreme disapproval of a nighttime high-speed chase while discussing an incident involving a white individual. He then makes racially charged comments suggesting that greater outrage would be warranted if it involved someone other than a white person, culminating in a discussion about Penn & Teller’s Broadway show and a caller's experience with a similar pursuit.

topics.title: Sports Contracts, Horse Abuse & Cher's Fitness Book
topics.summary: This broadcast discusses Bo Jackson’s contract issues with the Kansas City Royals and allegations of sexual assault involving horses. The conversation then shifts to Pen & Teller’s ‘Refrigerator Tour’ and a fitness book written by Cher, focusing on her personal journey towards health and wellness.

topics.title: Fire Eating, Computer Specs, and a Million Dollar Offer
topics.summary: A conversation begins with discussions about fire-eating attire and potassium sulfate for creating flames, abruptly shifting to computer specifications including an early 1980s ‘grid’ computer. The discussion then unexpectedly pivots towards Penn & Teller's Broadway show and a potential million-dollar endorsement deal for Howard Stern if he promotes cigarette brands.

topics.title: Zookeepers Play Instruments
topics.summary: During a radio segment, hosts discuss reports of zookeepers playing instruments and engaging in unusual activities. A guest reveals that Penn is now part of a band called 'Bongo's Bass & Bob,' performing at zoos while Howard expresses skepticism about the situation.
